decision_maker: Executive Cabinet
purpose:
Following a lengthy
procurement process, approval was needed for the contract award of
the new Open Framework for the transport of children with SEND to
school, children in social care and the transport of vulnerable
adults.

 

Local authorities had a legal
duty to provide free home-to-school transport for eligible children
of compulsory school age (5–16) who had special educational
needs and disabilities (SEND), where their needs or distance from
school make it necessary. The number of children receiving
transport support had more than doubled since the 2019/20 academic
year. In addition to the increase in demand, the average daily cost
per pupil had risen significantly from £31.84 to
£44.81, placing further pressure on the transport budget.
Adult Services had a legal duty to provide transport to clients who
were eligible for social care support in certain circumstances.
There were currently 118 individuals transported with external
providers funded by Adult Services.

 

Following approval at
Executive Cabinet on 24 September2025 the council started
procurement in collaboration with STAR, our procurement partner,
for a new framework for transport for these groups. The procurement
process had now concluded, and the new framework is now live. If
approved the framework will be for eight years. It would be
reopened at least twice during that period to allow other suppliers
to apply and encourage further competition.

decision_maker: Executive Cabinet
purpose:
This report sought approval
for the delegation of authority to either the Director of Strategic
Growth, or Head of Planning and Transportation, to agree and sign
Statements of Common Ground (SoCG) on behalf of the Council.
Statements of Common Ground are formal documents used within the
planning system to record matters of agreement and disagreement
between parties, particularly in the context of local plan
examinations and public inquiries.

 

The Council was currently
engaged in, several plan-making processes and
infrastructure-related examinations and inquiries, including the
forthcoming examination of the LocalPlan (Homes, Spaces, Places)
and the TransPennine Route Upgrade (TRU) public inquiry. These
processes operate to strict statutory and procedural timetables and
require timely officer engagement and sign-off. The Council’s
Constitution is currently silent on delegated authority
specifically relating to SoCG, which presents a risk of delay and
inefficiency to those processes.

the model to deliver in groupings more recognisable to the
Borough’s nine town communities and with resourcing models
that supports greater leadership and effective delivery of the
forums, improving town based engagement on Council
priorities.

develop, test and evolve an updated approach and any further
delivery requirements from impending legislation. Additionally,
during the transitional year the forums and community networks will

applications for Pride in Place Impact Fund proposals to deliver

decision_maker: Executive Cabinet
purpose:
This report seeks approval for the
Council to complete two strategic land acquisitions, defined as
Strategic Asset 1 and Strategic Asset 2, in support of the
long-term regeneration of Ashton Town Centre and proposals to
create a Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC). The Council has
completed its due diligence in respect of Strategic Asset 1, and is
about to commence the due diligence in respect of Strategic Asset
2. The Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) will be
providing a loan towards 50% of the acquisition costs.

 

The Council and Greater Manchester
(GM) have identified the Ashton Growth Corridor, comprising Ashton
Town Centre, St Petersfield, and the Ashton Moss employment area as
a priority area to deliver growth. The location forms part of the
GM Eastern Growth Cluster, which is one of six Growth Locations
across GM that will deliver new development, create and retain
jobs, offer better job opportunities, enable training and skill
development to increase the number of residents in
employment.

 

To support the delivery of these
ambitions the Ashton Mayoral Development Zone (AMDZ) has previously
been established as a strategic partnership between the Council,
the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) and key partners
including Homes England and Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM)
to drive forward the delivery of inclusive growth. The Council and
GMCA are currently progressing the work required to support the
creation of an Ashton and Stalybridge Mayoral Development
Corporation (MDC) to provide a national exemplar for transport-led
regeneration with a focus on accelerating housing and commercial
growth around existing and planned transport
infrastructure.

 

In August 2025 the Council’s
Executive Cabinet approved the Ashton Town Centre Vision &
Spatial Framework (the Framework) and exploration of potential
strategic site acquisitions in the Town Centre. The Framework has
identified the potential to deliver an estimated 2,400 new homes,
commercial and leisure facilities and comprehensive transport led
regeneration.

 

The Council has adopted a
pro-active intervention approach progressing strategic site
acquisitions in the Town Centre which will allow it to take a
longer-term view of regeneration without the commercial pressures
of private market expectations. This will unlock the opportunity
for Ashton Town Centre to provide a new ‘city-living’
residential market which can capitalise on excellent public
transport links into East Manchester and the
city-centre.

purpose:
The Community Parenting Strategy
sets out Tameside’s commitment to fulfilling our
responsibilities to children and young people in our care and to
care leavers. It outlines the principles and expectations that
ensure they receive the support, opportunities and care that any
good parent would provide.

 

The strategy is underpinned by our
Heart of Support Practice Approach, which informs how we build
relationships, understand lived experiences and work alongside
children, young people and families. Embedding this approach
strengthens our focus on promoting safety, wellbeing and positive
outcomes.

The strategy has been renamed from
the Corporate Parenting Strategy to the Community Parenting

decision_maker: Executive Member (Finance & Resources), First Deputy (Population Health and Wellbeing)
purpose:
The Greater Manchester Combined
Authority (GMCA) has awarded grant funding of £0.350m for
2025/26 to the Council to support the development and delivery of
an Enhanced Live Well Offer as part of the wider Live Well
programme.  
The grant award is to specifically
deliver the provision of dedicated support for people facing
multiple disadvantage.

 

The programme will fund a dedicated
programme with joint leadership from Public Health, Homelessness
and Adult Services to provide holistic support to those with
complex needs alongside preventative, community-based
support.

 

This will require the establishment
of an additional Live Well centre focussed on those who may have
early risks around housing and income needs, which can lead to
further issues if not addressed.  This Live Well centre will be facilitated by
the housing and homelessness teams and will provide open access,
preventative support. The other element of this programme is a
step-up enhanced holistic, multi-disciplinary team which will wrap
around the Live Well centre for those requiring further
support.  The proposal was submitted as an expression of
interest to the GMCA in January 2026 (see Appendix and has been
subsequently approved.  This will be supported by Making Every Adult
Matter who have been commissioned by the GMCA to enable delivery of
this programme in GM boroughs.

decision_maker: Executive Member (Finance & Resources), First Deputy (Population Health and Wellbeing)
purpose:
Greater Manchester Combined
Authority (GMCA) has provided funding of £0.132m for 2025-26
to Tameside Council to support the continued delivery of the Ageing
in Place project.

 

Ageing in Place is an approach that
creates the right conditions for older adults to thrive in their
communities, to live well at home and to access support at the
right time and at the right place.  
 This currently takes place at a local level,
supported by the Ageing Hub at the GMCA (Greater Manchester
Combined Authority), and has strong links to the Live Well
model.    Jigsaw Homes are the lead delivery partner and
the local authority Public Health team the senior sponsor for this
work.

 

This report seeks permission to
accept the grant funding from GMCA to come into the Public Health
budget and be allocated to Jigsaw Support as a contribution towards
the delivery of the Ageing in Place project.

purpose:
The Supported Housing (Regulatory
Oversight) Act 2023 places a statutory requirement on all Local
Authorities in England to create and implement a Supported Housing
Strategy.

To support this, MHCLG has
allocated £39 million for Local Authorities to develop their
strategies between 2025 and 2029.  Of this, £19 million has been designated
for 2025/26 to enable authorities to assess the current provision
of all types of supported housing in their area and forecast the
likely level of need over the five years following publication of
the strategy.

The Council has been allocated
£61,139 of new burdens grant funding, set out in a Memorandum
of Understanding (MoU).  Upon signing of the MoU (Appendix 1) and acceptance of the new burdens funding,
MHCLG will issue a Grant Determination letter setting out the
financial terms and conditions under Section 31 grants.

The Council will then commit to
spending the full allocation by the end of the 2026/27 financial
year.

decision_maker: Deputy Leader (Growth, Housing and Homelessness), Executive Member (Finance & Resources)
purpose:
The Emergency Accommodation
Reduction Pilot (EARP) is a national MHCLG programme which was
initially launched in January 2025 with a £5m fund allocated
to support the 20 local authorities experiencing the highest
pressures in reducing their reliance on B&B accommodation for
homeless families.  The programme aims to increase operational
capacity and strengthen prevention pathways.

In November 2025, MHCLG announced
an uplift of £2.5m and confirmed that Tameside Housing Advice
had been selected to receive additional funding to undertake an
occupancy audit.  This decision was based on HCLIC data published
in June 2025, which recorded 10 or more households with children
placed in B&B accommodation beyond the statutory six-week
limit, and because Tameside was not included in the original pilot
cohort.

The grant provides £150,000
to carry out an audit to identify any voids, fraud, or irregular
arrangements, with the intention of freeing up units for households
currently placed in the most unsuitable forms of temporary
accommodation.
